gdc/singletons/audio.html.title: Audio
gdc/singletons/audio.html.description:
first you have to load the sounds you need using Audio.load_sounds()
then you play the sound using Audio.play_sound()extends Control const sounds = [ "alert" ] func _ready() -> void: Audio.load_sounds(sounds) await get_tree().create_timer(1).timeout Audio.play_sound("alert") Parameters: Array[String] use: it's to load sounds in scene changing so assets don't overload the RAMHow to use Audio.load_sounds(sounds) Parameters: String use: It's for developers to play loaded soundsHow to use Audio.play_sound("sound_name")
The sound library is inside a variable in Audio.

gdc/singletons/segue.html.title: Segue
gdc/singletons/segue.html.description: you only have to do Audio.change_scene().extends Control func _ready() -> void: Segue.change_scene(Segue.MAIN_SCENE) # or Segue.change_scene("res://Scenes/main/main.tscn") Parameters: String, String use: it's to change to scenes in a more graceful way rather than an instant change.How to use you can use it with the default transition Segue.change_scene("path/to/scene") # or Segue.change_scene(Segue.MAIN_SCENE) or you can use a specific transition animation Segue.change_scene("path/to/scene", "dissolve") # or Segue.change_scene(Segue.MAIN_SCENE, Segue.DISSOLVE_TRANSITION) The Scenes and Transitions are constant variables inside Segue.

gdc/chapter-1-game-jam.html.title: Chapter 1 - Game Jam
gdc/chapter-1-game-jam.html.description: Created the Audio and Segue singletons for everyone to use.Agawan is a fast-paced 3v3 / 4v4 top-down(subject to change) multiplayer arena title that transforms the traditional Visayan street game Tayukok (Agawan Base) into a high-stakes, competitive esports experience. The game fuses the core tagging and rescue mechanics of traditional street play with a circular-economy resource race and mechanical movement systems.Themes: Philippine Games and Sports & Circular Economy Genere: Top-Down(subject to change) Competitive Action / Team Tag Arena Platform: PC / Android (Gamepad and Keyboard/Mouse support) Match format: 3v3 or 4v4, best-of-3 sets (2-3 minutes per round) Visual Style: ???To eliminate camping and reward mechanical execution, player navigation is governed by active resource management and split-second evasion tools.Omnidirectional Sprint: Consumes a 100-point Stamina Meter over 3.5 seconds of sustained sprinting. Stamina regenerates rapidly only when walking or standing still. Complete depletion causes an "Exhaustion" state, locking sprint and dash for 1.2 seconds. Tactical Dash: Consumes 35 stamina or uses 1 of 2 discrete dash charges on a short 4-second cooldown. Grants Grants 0.18 seconds of invulnerability frames (I-frames). During an active dash, incoming tag hitboxes are nullified Allows agile players to dodge through an aggressive chaser’s forward lunge, causing the attacker to miss, slide, and overshoot their momentum. Weight and Encumbrance Penalties: Carrying scrap nodes or power batteries reduces baseline movement speed by 15% and accelerates sprint stamina drain by 25% Runners cannot simply grab scrap and sprint home untouched; they require defensive screens, peelers, or coordinated lane handoffs. Tag Combat: The "Fresh Touch" Priority Engine: Tag mechanics rely entirely on the traditional Tayukok "freshness" rule, driven by server-authoritative timestamps to ensure competitive fairness.Base Step-Off -> Timestamp Locked -> Visual Aura Assigned -> Tag Combat Tag Priority (Freshness): Stepping outside the home base border locks a player's Exit Timestamp. Any player who steps onto the field after an opponent gains Predator Advantage over that specific opponent. If Player A leaves base at 0:10 and Player B leaves base at 0:12, Player B can tag and eliminate Player A on contact. Visual Status Telegraphing Predator Aura(Sharp/Hilighted): indicates priority over target opponents within proximity Prey Aura (Dim/Pulsing Warning): Alerts the player that an active enemy on the field is fresher and poses an immediate capture threat. Clash / Parity (Equal Timestamps): If two opposing players exit within 0.25 seconds of each other, physical contact triggers an explosive knockback wave rather than an elimination, resetting both players' momentum. Anti-Stall Duration: Stepping off the base grants predatory priority for a maximum of 15 seconds. Once the timer expires, the aura decays to neutral status, forcing players to either retreat to touch their home boundary or risk being tagged by any active enemy. Capture, Jail & The "Kuryente" Chain Rescue The Holding Cell: Tagged players are teleported to the enemy’s containment grid adjacent to their base. The Living Chain (Kuryente): Captured teammates can physically link hands, forming a connected tether reaching out toward the neutral zone. Each additional prisoner lengthens the chain, bringing the rescue point closer to mid-lane. The High-Stakes Breakout: If an active teammate dashes past defenders and touches any segment of the prisoner chain without being tagged: All imprisoned players are instantly liberated. Rescued players receive a 2.5-second phase shield (invulnerability + bonus movespeed) to reposition back to neutral territory. Role Archetypes(Subject to change) Teams assemble rosters using three distinct player roles.Win Conditions and Esports Match Loop Rounds last between 2 and 3 minutes, driven by three definitive win conditions Reactor Meltdown (Resource Starvation): A team’s base Eco-Reactor naturally ticks downward. Failure to collect and deposit recycled batteries from the center lane causes the base core to hit 0%, ending the round in defeat. Base Infiltration (Overload Tap) A runner carrying an overcharged energy core successfully touches the enemy team's main reactor terminal. Total Team Wipe (Prisoner Lockdown All players of an opposing team are trapped in the holding cell simultaneously.

Form: https://nstw-competition.dostncr.ph/register/level-up-3 After discussing the above we are now in the stage for the members to tell their game idea to the team so that all of us can see which game is good to make. Can we make it in a week? Is it easy to make? Will normies enjoy it? Are you willing to make it? Esports Potential? Smart City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Climate Change Education Circular Economy Philippine Games and Sports Board Games / Brain Games Networking Game smart city education Dakpanay / tayukok Philippine Games Esports Characters possible moba Philippine Mayor Simulator disaster risk reduction and management. Pinoy fighting game has potential but not allowed Once the majority has agreed on what game to make. it's time to address the roles of each team memberWith the roles that we now have, we'll have to plan on what to make in the game. the vision us developers want to make is the full game. from start to finish. Theme Mechanics Features User Friendliness Musical Direction Art Style with all finished and planned, everybody having their role and confidence in place. we now ask questions to our fellow members to discuss some confusion from the meeting.
now that everybody is satisfied. Prologue - The Meeting will now come to a close.

info_showOrphanNodes.description: Show nodes that are not connected to any other nodes.

info_showAttachments.description: Show attachments like images and PDFs as nodes in the graph.

info_allowGlobalGraph.description: Allow the user to view the global graph of all nodes.

info_allowExpand.description: Allow the user to pop-out the graph view to take up the whole screen

info_attractionForce.description: How much should linked nodes attract each other? This will make the graph appear more clustered.

info_linkLength.description: How long should the links between nodes be? The shorter the links the more connected nodes will cluster together.

info_repulsionForce.description: How much should nodes repel each other? This will make disconnected parts more spread out.

info_centralForce.description: How much should nodes be attracted to the center? This will make the graph appear more dense and circular.

info_edgePruning.description: Edges with a length above this threshold will not be rendered, however they will still contribute to the simulation. This can help large tangled graphs look more organised. Hovering over a node will still display these links.

info_minNodeRadius.description: How small should the smallest nodes be? The smaller a node is the less it will attract other nodes.

info_maxNodeRadius.description: How large should the largest nodes be? Nodes are sized by how many links they have. The larger a node is the more it will attract other nodes. This can be used to create a good grouping around the most important nodes.
